As of this check it displays "Formulario cerrado" (form closed) — the 2025-26 window (Sept 23 - Oct 3, 2025) has passed and next cycle's dates aren't posted yet, but this is the real application entry point to check again when it reopens.

name: FIRST LEGO League Euskadi (Innobasque, with BBK & Iberdrola)
org: Innobasque (Basque Innovation Agency), sponsored by BBK, Iberdrola & Basque Government departments
description: The Basque Country's regional FLL program, run since 2009 by the Basque government's innovation agency with three Basque universities, funded by sponsors including BBK and Iberdrola, plus regional education/innovation ministries.
amount: Free regional tournament participation + sponsor-funded company/research-center visits
details: Not a cash grant to individual teams — funding covers running the regional tournament (held simultaneously in Bilbao, Donostia, Mondragón & Vitoria-Gasteiz) and unique sponsor-arranged visits to companies and technology/research centers tied to each year's challenge theme. Enroll through the national FIRST LEGO League Spain (Ingeniera Soy) site.

name: Vodafone Romania FTC Co-Sponsorship
description: Vodafone Romania is the co-namesake sponsor of "BRD FIRST Tech Challenge Romania powered by Vodafone," providing an estimated €280,000 in free kits and equipment across the program's 48 participating high schools.
amount: Part of ~€280,000 in program-wide kits/equipment (shared across all enrolled teams, not per-team cash)
details: Funding flows through the national program (register via Nație prin Educație, listed separately) rather than a direct per-team Vodafone application — Vodafone's support covers free kits/equipment and webinars/training access for all enrolled teams rather than cash grants.

name: TurkNet FRC Türkiye Communications Sponsorship
description: TurkNet has served as the recurring communications/technology sponsor of FIRST Robotics Competition Türkiye for multiple consecutive years, providing fiber internet support for the national event.
amount: Event-level communications/infrastructure sponsorship (not a per-team cash grant)
details: This is national-event infrastructure sponsorship (fast, uninterrupted internet for the competition) rather than team-facing funding — there's no separate team application. Contact FRC Türkiye directly about the event and its sponsor list. Note: the original frcturkiye.org/sponsorlar/ link 404s — this points to TurkNet's own FRC sponsorship page instead.

name: Türk-Alman Üniversitesi & Siemens FRC Türkiye Support
description: Mentoring, workshop-facility access, and sponsorship support offered to FRC teams competing in a Turkish regional, run jointly by Türk-Alman Üniversitesi and Siemens.
amount: In-kind: mentoring, workshop access + sponsorship support
details: Mentoring, workshop-facility access, and sponsorship support offered to FRC teams competing in a Turkish regional, run jointly by Türk-Alman Üniversitesi and Siemens. Requires participating in an FRC Regional competition in Turkey to qualify. The frcturkiye.org/hibeler/ page names a specific application deadline (Sept 19, 2025 in the most recently documented cycle) and links to further application details from that page itself — but the underlying direct-application URL isn't a stable, separately linkable page, so check frcturkiye.org/hibeler/ each year and click through from there for the current window's specific form.

name: Vishwakarma University FTC India Scholarship
description: Vishwakarma University, title sponsor of the FIRST Tech Challenge India Championship, introduced scholarships in 2024-25 for students who participate in or volunteer at the event.
amount: Varies (scholarship for participating/volunteering students)
details: Announced by Dr. Siddharth Jabade at the 2024-25 championship inauguration: "From this year, Vishwakarma University will offer scholarships to students participating and volunteering in the event." This is separate from the general FTC India Sponsor-a-Student program — contact FTC India or Vishwakarma University directly for current scholarship terms, since the announcement didn't specify a fixed amount or a standalone application form.

name: FTC India Championship Robotics Kit Sponsorship (Bajaj Auto & Partners)
org: Bajaj Auto Ltd. (with John Deere, Dow, RTX & InfinityX STEM Foundation)
description: Bajaj Auto Ltd. joined other corporate sponsors to fund 20 robotics kits for FTC India Championship students from economically disadvantaged backgrounds, a recurring commitment across multiple championship years.
amount: 20 sponsored robotics kits per championship cycle (shared across sponsors)
details: This is a championship-level in-kind kit donation coordinated by InfinityX STEM Foundation (India's FTC Program Delivery Partner) rather than a per-team application — teams from rural areas, municipal-corporation schools, and remote regions (Ladakh, Assam, Dharavi) have been past recipients. Contact InfinityX STEM Foundation or FTC India directly to ask about eligibility for the next championship cycle.

name: SARAO FIRST LEGO League Northern Cape Support
description: SARAO's Human Capital Development Programme hosts and supports FIRST LEGO League regional and provincial competitions across the Northern Cape, and has funded specific teams' travel to international FLL championships (Morocco Open, FLL Open Africa).
amount: Varies (event hosting, judging/volunteer support, and travel funding for select teams to international events)
details: SARAO runs this as part of its long-standing Schools Programme in the Northern Cape (tied to the Square Kilometre Array project's local community investment), partnering with Tshwane University of Technology and UNISA's I-SET — it isn't an open online application, so schools in the Northern Cape (Carnarvon, Williston, Loxton, Vosburg, Sutherland, Brandvlei, Kimberley) should contact SARAO's Schools Programme directly to get involved.

name: FIRST LEGO League Korea Sponsors & Partners
org: Imagine Association (with Cubroid, Dong-A Science & other Korean partners)
description: FIRST LEGO League Korea lists its current season sponsors and partner organizations, including robotics-kit maker Cubroid and science media outlet Dong-A Science, alongside academic and industry partners.
amount: Varies (event-level sponsorship, not per-team funding)
details: This is national tournament-level sponsorship rather than a per-team grant — the page itself notes FLL Korea is actively seeking additional sponsors and partners. Contact Imagine Association (fll.korea@imagine.or.kr) about current partnership opportunities for schools.

name: Dassault Systèmes & La Fondation Dassault Systèmes Partnership
org: Dassault Systèmes / La Fondation Dassault Systèmes
description: Key partners of Robotique FIRST France since its founding in 2022, providing free SOLIDWORKS and 3DEXPERIENCE software licenses to French student teams alongside broader program support.
amount: In-kind: free SOLIDWORKS desktop, SOLIDWORKS Cloud Apps & 3DEXPERIENCE platform licenses
details: This is a software and program-level partnership rather than a per-team cash grant — teams get free access to Dassault Systèmes' CAD tools through Robotique FIRST France's program setup, not a separate application. The partnership has run since Robotique FIRST France's first season and is credited alongside EDF and the Gene Haas Foundation as a backer of the national Défi Robotique final.

name: Syntec-Ingénierie & Concepteurs d'Avenirs Member Company Support
description: France's engineering-industry federation became a partner of Robotique FIRST France in March 2023, inviting member engineering firms to fund teams financially or contribute employee expertise as mentors.
amount: Varies by member company (financial support and/or employee mentoring)
details: There's no single federation-wide grant — individual Syntec-Ingénierie member firms (e.g. Vulcain Engineering Group, listed separately) choose whether to sponsor a team financially or send professionals to mentor students. Ask Robotique FIRST France whether a member firm is active near your team's region.

name: Vulcain Engineering Group Robotique FIRST France Sponsorship
description: A multi-year Robotique FIRST France partner that finances team equipment and mobilizes employees from several of its subsidiaries (VSER, Consultys, Infogene, Sofren Group, CCAMY Systems) as student mentors.
amount: Varies (equipment financing + employee mentors across project management, electrical engineering, mechanics & robotics)
details: No public per-team application — Vulcain has taken part for multiple consecutive seasons as a corporate partner. Reach out through Robotique FIRST France to ask whether Vulcain (or another Syntec-Ingénierie member) is supporting teams in your region this season.

name: Fondation Grenoble INP FIRST Tech Challenge Support
description: The foundation of the Grenoble Institute of Technology backs the French edition of FIRST Tech Challenge as an educational initiative, inviting organizations to become privileged partners of the competition.
amount: Varies; specific amounts not published
details: Public details on funding amounts, eligibility, or an application process are not published on the foundation's page — contact Fondation Grenoble INP directly through their site to ask about current-season support for FTC teams, particularly those near Grenoble.

name: FPL Robotics Team Grant & Scholarship
description: FPL directly sponsors FIRST, VEX, and B.E.S.T. robotics teams across its Florida service territory, funding travel and competition costs, plus a separate $20,000 FIRST Robotics Scholarship for a graduating senior with 2+ years on a team.
amount: Varies (team grants); $20,000 one-time scholarship (separate program, opens ~Feb-April)
details: Apply through STEM2 Hub's online form with an FPL request-for-funding form and W-9; allow up to 45 days for processing and payment. Only public, private, and charter school teams within FPL's Florida service territory qualify (check FPL's coverage map) — community clubs outside the territory are not eligible, and teams must have existed for over a year. Budget caps apply each season and funds are not replenished once exhausted. The separate $20,000 scholarship is for graduating seniors, not teams directly.

name: Walmart & Sam's Club Spark Good Local Grants
description: General community grants ($250-$5,000) from individual Walmart stores, Sam's Clubs, and Distribution Centers to local 501(c)(3) nonprofits and schools — not robotics-specific, but explicitly open to STEM/technology education uses.
details: This is a general community-grant program, not a dedicated FIRST/robotics fund — your team (or its fiscal sponsor, e.g. a school or booster club) applies as any local nonprofit would. Requires a verified Spark Good account via Walmart's Deed platform. Three application cycles per fiscal year: Feb 1-Apr 15, May 1-Jul 15, and Aug 1-Nov 30. Funding comes from the specific local store/club/DC nearest your team, not a national pool.

name: Costco Wholesale Charitable Contributions
description: General community grants (up to $5,000) for 501(c)(3) nonprofits working in children, education, or health/human services — not robotics-specific, but a real, open application usable by a school-sponsored or booster-club-backed FIRST team.
amount: Up to $5,000 (capped at 10% of your program budget)
details: Not a FIRST-specific program — Costco funds children's/education/health nonprofits generally, reviewed on a rolling basis (one request per fiscal year, Sept 1-Aug 31). Apply online with a cover letter and budget documents; decisions take 4-6 weeks. Your team needs 501(c)(3) status itself or a fiscal sponsor (school, booster club) that has it, and framing your application around measurable educational outcomes matters more than mentioning robotics specifically.

name: Publix Charities Community Giving Request
description: General donation/sponsorship request program for youth and education nonprofits in Publix's operating region — not robotics-specific, but real and open to school/booster-club-backed FIRST teams.
amount: Varies (donations, gift cards, sponsorships, or program ads; amounts not published)
details: General donation/sponsorship request program for youth and education nonprofits in Publix's operating region — not robotics-specific, but real and open to school/booster-club-backed FIRST teams. There is no single fixed-URL application form — corporate.publix.com/community/requests is the correct starting landing page, which routes to a "Request Support" flow (and, separately, publixcharities.org for larger nonprofit grant requests); an organization representative registers there to submit the request. Only available in Publix's operating states.

name: Kroger Community Rewards
description: A passive fundraising mechanism (not a competitive grant) where shoppers link their Kroger card to a chosen nonprofit, including FIRST teams like FRC Team 862 (Lightning Robotics), and a share of their grocery spending is donated automatically.
amount: Varies (small % of enrolled shoppers' purchases; no cap on team enrollment)
details: This isn't a grant application — it's a low-effort, ongoing revenue-share: register your team as a nonprofit organization on Kroger's Community Rewards platform, then have supporters link the program to their Kroger Plus/digital account. Only meaningful in states with Kroger-family stores (Kroger, Ralphs, Fred Meyer, King Soopers, etc.), and payouts are small per-shopper but recur automatically with no reapplication needed.
